notes: Reviewed the actual commit diff (f33c7ee) in this worktree, not the prior summary. Scope is narrow: AbortController-based cancellation added to Browse's fetchListings, plus an optional `signal` param threaded through api.ts's `get()` and `listingsApi.getAll()`. No new endpoints, no auth/authorization changes, no change to what data is returned or to whom (still the same public GET /listings call, already covered by optionalAuth and the global rate limiter). The signal is only ever attached to a same-origin GET fetch with existing credentials handling unchanged; aborting a superseded request cannot be used to bypass rate limiting, since the request is still sent before being aborted (network cancellation, not request suppression), and the existing requestIdRef sequencing guard (from a prior task) was already sufficient to prevent the stale-response append bug described in the QA finding — this change only adds efficiency, not new attack surface. No secrets, tokens, or PII touched by this diff. No XSS/CSRF/injection surface introduced. No admin/moderation code involved.
